documentation.purpose: The deployment contract for miner-fleet: what this application needs from whatever packages it. Generated by tools/deploymentContract.ts from src/config/runtimeConfig.ts (runtimeConfigDefaults plus the exported *_ENV constants), docker/Dockerfile (ENV PORT and EXPOSE), and the health route module's own position in Next's file-system routing. Regenerate with `npm run contract:generate`. This file is never hand-edited; a regenerate-and-diff test fails the suite, naming the drifted field, when it is stale relative to those sources. RichardWilliams/miner-fleet-store ASSERTS its packaging against this file. This repo never generates, templates, or emits any part of that repo's compose file, and that direction is permanent.
documentation.requiredEnvKeysMeaning: requiredEnvKeys names the keys WITHOUT WHICH THE CONTAINER FAILS TO START. That reading is forced rather than merely preferred: the store supplies environment through an operator-owned env file it declares optional, so it cannot guarantee that any key is present at all. Under the competing reading — "the application is not functional without it" — the subnet key would land in this set, the store could not satisfy the contract, and every release would be blocked. The set is empty, and that is the honest answer rather than a gap: the application starts and serves the health path with an entirely empty environment, every tunable falling back to a default that ships inside the image.
documentation.packagingAffecting: The facts the packaging itself depends on: the port the container listens on, the path a health check must probe, the environment key naming the directory state is written to together with its default, and the required key set. A change to any of them needs a coordinated bump on the packaging side. The data-directory key sits here rather than among the tunables because overriding it without a matching change to the mount on the packaging side writes state to an unmounted path, which is discarded on the next restart.
documentation.nonPackagingAffecting: Tunables the operator may set through the on-box env file with no packaging change at all; adding a key here never requires a coordinated release. The data-directory key is deliberately absent from this set — see packagingAffecting. No per-key defaults are published: the tunable defaults ship inside the image, and there is no derivable key-to-default mapping to emit, so publishing them would mean hand-writing the second copy this contract exists to remove. functionalImpactWhenUnset, where present, records what the application does without the key while still starting normally.

optionalEnvKeys.functionalImpactWhenUnset: The fleet is empty until this key names the ranges to sweep. Left unset, discovery derives the sweep range from the container's own non-internal IPv4 address, which under this packaging is the Docker app network rather than the operator's own network — so the application starts and serves normally while finding no miners. There is deliberately no default range: a guessed one is wrong on most networks and produces that same empty fleet while looking identical to broken discovery.
